items.title: Vyasa – A client-side AI writing detector (WASM, no API calls)
items.raw_excerpt:
Now that Wikipedia has banned AI generated articles. - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Writing_articles_wit... I wanted to try and see if it was possible to get somewhat decent engine based on signs of AI writing from wikipedia themselves. It runs entirely in the browser via WASM. Added instructions to further add more ways to figure out as we find out more about LLMs. Would love feedback!!, especially:
- cases where it completely fails
- patterns you think are stronger indicators
- whether this approach is even worth pursuing vs proper ML models, considering this is a classical classification task, I just don't like the idea of detection of a black box with another black box.

title_i18n.en: Vyasa – A client-side AI writing detector (WASM, no API calls)
title_i18n.zh: 维雅萨——一款客户端AI写作检测器（基于WASM，无需API调用）
title_i18n.es: Vyasa – Un detector de escritura con IA en el lado del cliente (WASM, sin llamadas a API).

excerpt_i18n.en:
Now that Wikipedia has banned AI generated articles. - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Writing_articles_wit... I wanted to try and see if it was possible to get somewhat decent engine based on signs of AI writing from wikipedia themselves. It runs entirely in the browser via WASM. Added instructions to further add more ways to figure out as we find out more about LLMs. Would love feedback!!, especially:
- cases where it completely fails
- patterns you think are stronger indicators
- whether this approach is even worth pursuing vs proper ML models, considering this is a classical classification task, I just don't like the idea of detection of a black box with another black box.
excerpt_i18n.zh: 维基百科现已禁止AI生成文章。我想尝试看看，能否基于AI写作的迹象打造出尚可的引擎。
excerpt_i18n.es: Ahora que Wikipedia ha prohibido los artículos generados por IA. - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Writing_articles_wit... Quería intentar ver si era posible conseguir un motor algo decente basado en indicios de escritura de IA.

items.title: How are you keeping AI coding agents from burning money?
